brief: SpaceX's agreement to buy up to 14 MHz of 800MHz spectrum from Grain Management removed Starlink's walls-penetration defense, so the Big Three wireless carriers had their worst single-session equity decline in a decade (TMUS -13%, T -10%, VZ -9%) and IG credit spreads widened 7-10bp, closing at the wides on thin Friday liquidity. Goldman's credit desk maps four management responses: do nothing (credit negative, slow terminal-value bleed), buy defensive spectrum (credit negative, leverage rises), strike a wholesale deal with SpaceX (credit positive but term-dependent), or let SpaceX acquire a carrier outright (credit negative regardless, since change-of-control puts need a downgrade below investment grade to trigger). Three of four paths are leverage-increasing or negative for bonds, so the real driver is which option management picks on upcoming earnings calls: deleverage (credit-positive, equity-negative, the cable playbook), fight via auctions and M&A (credit-negative), or consolidate (mixed). A ratings-agency re-rating could hit years before cash flow does. Bull case: telco spreads screen cheap, yields above 7%, subscriber erosion years away. Goldman's bottom line calls this a curve-steepening event, not a near-term default risk.
